description: The AUTOPILOT project partners publish connected-driving logs from an 11.6-kilometre roadworks demonstration near Livorno, Italy. Zenodo supplies seven archives free under CC BY 4.0. One automated vehicle and two connected vehicles exchanged roadside and cloud messages using ITS-G5, oneM2M and an electronic-horizon service. Logged variables include GPS, speed, steering and battery signals together with roadwork notifications and map or hazard messages. These records can benchmark communication and vehicle-response components in traffic digital twins. Related G6 data-autopilot-brainport-roadside-camera-obstacle-logs covers a separate Dutch test-track demonstration. Coverage is the documented Italian scenarios, not representative national traffic. Timing alignment and operational context are needed to interpret responses; notification receipt alone does not demonstrate safety improvement. No archive was downloaded or latency and behaviour results reproduced. Additional source-linked AUTOPILOT highway sessions cover different automated/connected-vehicle combinations, connected-car pre-tests and speed adaptation for roadworks or puddle hazards. Described loops are 11.6 km for roadwork tests and 12.3 km for puddle scenarios. All seven deposits retain independent native identities and archive descriptors. The 3630462 description concerns puddles while its listed archive names concern roadworks; exact session content remains unresolved. The 3630456 roadwork pre-test also lists a puddle-named component. These are explicit metadata conflicts, not proof of identical trials. CAN/GPS, V2X and oneM2M content categories are common, but no common sample interval or reproduced safety result is established.
